author: zusez4
body:
<!-- homu-ignore:start -->
*[View all comments](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-comments/rust-lang/rust/pull/150683)*
<!-- homu-ignore:end -->

This intrinsic helps with supporting the various AMD & NVIDIA libraries like rocBLAS or cuBLAS.
They provide functions which *must* be called from the host, but require a mixture of host and device pointers.
This offload_args intrinsic maps our host allocations to device allocations and transfers memory as required.
It reuses the whole infrastructure which we already have for the main offload intrinsic.
Unlike the main offload intrinsic, this also already fully works with std. I also got it to work with a single cargo invocation:
`RUSTFLAGS="-L native=/opt/rocm-6.4.0/lib -l dylib=rocblas -l dylib=amdhip64 -l dylib=omp -l dylib=omptarget -Zoffload=Args -Zunstable-options"  cargo +offload run -r`


I'll rebase and drop the first 3 commits once the cleanup PR lands.

I updated `compiler/rustc_monomorphize/src/collector/autodiff.rs`, it now works without no_mangle, otherwise the function won't be codegen'ed. It also works without lto=fat if we only have main.rs
If we put a function in lib.rs and call it in main.rs, then it currently trips the verifier. Happy to fix it either here or in a follow-up PR:
```
thread 'rustc' (494962) panicked at compiler/rustc_monomorphize/src/collector.rs:468:13:
assertion failed: tcx.should_codegen_locally(instance)
stack backtrace:
```

cc @Kevinsala @Sa4dUs

author: dinesh-git17
body:
## Summary

Phase 6 foundation implementing the Binary Search Tree visualization domain. This PR covers Stories 6.1–6.3, establishing the data architecture, renderer, and core BST operations.

### Story 6.1 — Tree Architecture (Store Refactor)
- Add `tree` to `VisualizerMode` type
- Define `TreeNode` interface with flat/normalized state pattern (id references instead of nested objects)
- Add `TreeState` with `rootId` and `nodes` lookup map for O(1) access
- Add `TreeAlgorithmType` for operations (`insert`, `search`, `delete`) and traversals
- Implement store actions: `insertNode`, `deleteNode`, `resetTree`, `setTreeState`
- Add `TREE_CONFIG` constants and helper functions

### Story 6.2 — Elastic Stage (Tree Renderer)
- Build `TreeStage.tsx` with binary split layout algorithm
- Layout: Root at X=50%, each level halves remaining width
- SVG layer for edge lines with draw animation (pathLength)
- Framer Motion circles for nodes with pop animation (scale: 0→1)
- Empty state hint with tree emoji
- Wire `Canvas.tsx` to render `TreeStage` in tree mode

### Story 6.3 — BST Operations (Core Logic)
- Define `TreeStep` discriminated union types:
  - `compare` — comparing node value with target
  - `visit` — visiting during traversal
  - `insert` — new node inserted
  - `found` — value found (green pulse)
  - `not-found` — value not in tree (red shake)
  - `delete` — node deletion with strategy
  - `traverse-output` — traversal output with order
- Implement BST operation generators:
  - `bstInsert` — yields compare steps, then insert
  - `bstSearch` — yields compare steps, then found/not-found
  - `bstDelete` — handles leaf, one-child, two-children cases
- Implement traversal generators:
  - `inOrderTraversal` — Left → Root → Right (sorted)
  - `preOrderTraversal` — Root → Left → Right
  - `postOrderTraversal` — Left → Right → Root
  - `levelOrderTraversal` — BFS level-by-level

### UI Integration
- Enable Trees mode in sidebar navigation
- Add tree algorithm list (Insert, Search, Delete, traversals)
- Update `ComplexityModal` to handle tree mode descriptions

## Test plan

- [x] 19 unit tests for store operations (insertNode, deleteNode, resetTree)
- [x] 23 unit tests for BST generators (insert, search, delete, all traversals)
- [x] All 216 tests passing
- [x] TypeScript strict mode passes
- [x] Build succeeds
- [x] Manual: Click "Trees" in sidebar → shows empty tree state
- [x] Manual: Sidebar shows tree operations and traversals list

## Next Steps

Story 6.5 (Tree Control Deck) will add the input field, action buttons, and controller to wire up the generators with the UI.

author: koic
body:
## Motivation and Context

Unlike applications, libraries provide value by remaining usable for a broad range of users, even when that means supporting older Ruby versions beyond Ruby's own EOL timeline.

I maintain RuboCop, a Ruby linter. Because linters need to work across the ecosystem, they often need to keep compatibility with older Ruby versions to some extent.

The trade-off is that the MCP Ruby SDK must remain compatible with Ruby 2.7. However, given the ecosystem impact, supporting Ruby 2.7 is still worthwhile.

For example, bundled gems such as `csv` (Ruby >= 2.5), `bigdecimal` (Ruby >= 2.5), `json` (Ruby >= 2.7), and `language_server-protocol` (Ruby >= 2.5) tend to keep compatibility with older Ruby versions.

## How Has This Been Tested?

`rubocop-shopify` (2.18) supports Ruby 3.1+, and this PR does not change that. Since RuboCop can configure the runtime Ruby version and the target Ruby version for analysis independently, CI continues to run RuboCop on Ruby 4.0, while analyzing code with `TargetRubyVersion: 2.7`.

When setting `TargetRubyVersion: 2.7`, several RuboCop offenses were resolved.

Additionally, Sorbet-related libraries support Ruby 3.0+. Since these are not dependencies of the MCP Ruby SDK itself, they are versioned and tested in the development Gemfile.

New test matrix for up to Ruby 2.7 has been added to CI.

## Breaking Changes

Unlike dropping support, which imposes restrictions on users, this change broadens compatibility and does not introduce breaking changes.

## Types of changes
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: -->
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Checklist
<!-- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->

- [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines

body: This PR adds support for simplifying lambda expressions in `Sym.simp`. It is much more efficient than standard simp for very large lambda expressions with many binders. author: itsmontoya
body:
## Summary
- Add `scribble-server`: a streaming-first HTTP server for transcription with a small, explicit API surface.
- Refactor the library so a single loaded Whisper context can be reused concurrently across requests.

## Why
- We want Scribble to support long-running services and true streaming inputs (e.g. live/24hr streams) in addition to the CLI.
- We want concurrent transcriptions without forcing a global server mutex around the entire pipeline.

## Changes
- Add `src/bin/scribble-server.rs` with:
  - `GET /healthz`
  - `GET /v1/models`
  - `POST /v1/transcribe` using the raw request body as input and streaming the transcription output as the response body.
  - Bounded prefix probing + replay to fail fast on obviously unsupported inputs without buffering the full upload.
- Refactor backend ownership:
  - `Backend` APIs use `&self` (shared model contexts; per-request state is created per transcription).
  - `Scribble::transcribe` uses `&self`.
- VAD strategy:
  - Initialize VAD context per request (documented tradeoff; to revisit if/when upstream VAD context guarantees make reuse/pooling a better default).
- Streaming reader support:
  - Decoder/transcription pipeline accepts `Read + Send` readers that are not `Sync` (required for bridging async HTTP bodies into a dedicated decode thread).
- Documentation updates:
  - README server section + examples (no `incremental_min_window_seconds` knob exposed).
- Tests:
  - Add `tests/decoder_non_sync_reader.rs` to lock in support for `Send` but non-`Sync` readers.

## Behavior / API impact
- New binary: `scribble-server`.
- Server transcribe endpoint now accepts raw body bytes (streaming) rather than multipart.
- Library API changes:
  - `Scribble::transcribe` now takes `&self`.
  - `Backend` trait methods now take `&self`.
- VAD behavior in services: per-request init (potentially higher per-request overhead vs pooling).

## Edge cases considered
- Empty request body returns `400`.
- Unsupported/unrecognized container returns `415` before starting a streamed response.
- Mid-stream decode failures can’t change HTTP status once headers are sent; the stream will terminate early and the server logs the error.

## Testing
- [x] cargo fmt --all -- --check
- [x] cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
- [x] cargo test --all-features

## Follow-ups
- Consider a VAD pool and/or more explicit concurrency controls (worker pool sizing, backpressure, cancellation).
- Add integration tests for the HTTP server (status codes + streaming semantics) once we decide on test harness approach.

author: jmgilman
body:
## Summary

This PR makes devcontainers the primary and default method for running Headjack instances, with base container images as a fallback option.

### Key Changes

- **Rename `--base` to `--image`**: Clearer semantics that this bypasses devcontainer detection
- **Make `default.base_image` optional**: Defaults to empty instead of the base image
- **Add devcontainer CLI warning**: Always warns if the devcontainer CLI is not found in PATH
- **Error on missing configuration**: If no devcontainer.json exists and no image is configured, provide clear error with guidance
- **Remove `hjk recreate` command**: Users should use `hjk rm` + `hjk run` instead
- **Update documentation**: All docs now reflect devcontainer-first approach

### New Behavior

When running `hjk run`:
1. If `--image` is specified, use that image (bypasses devcontainer)
2. If `devcontainer.json` exists in the repo, use devcontainer mode automatically
3. If `default.base_image` is configured, use that as fallback
4. Otherwise, error with guidance on how to configure

### Breaking Changes

- `--base` flag renamed to `--image`
- `hjk recreate` command removed (use `hjk rm && hjk run` instead)
- `default.base_image` now defaults to empty (previously defaulted to `ghcr.io/gilmanlab/headjack:base`)

## Test plan

- [x] `just check` passes (fmt, lint, test)
- [ ] Manual testing of devcontainer detection
- [ ] Manual testing of `--image` flag
- [ ] Manual testing of error when no devcontainer or image configured

author: estif0
body:
This pull request introduces two new modules to the codebase for handling and preprocessing the CFPB complaints dataset. The first module, `CFPBDataLoader`, is responsible for robustly loading and validating the raw data. The second module, `DataPreprocessor`, provides a comprehensive pipeline for filtering, cleaning, and preparing the complaint narratives for downstream use. Together, these modules establish a structured and extensible foundation for data ingestion and preparation in the RAG pipeline.

**Data Loading and Validation:**

* Added `CFPBDataLoader` class in `src/data_loader.py` to encapsulate loading, validating, and basic inspection of the CFPB complaints dataset, including error handling, logging, and checks for required columns and duplicates.

**Data Preprocessing Pipeline:**

* Introduced `DataPreprocessor` class in `src/data_preprocessor.py` to filter complaints by product, remove empty narratives, and clean text data with customizable options (e.g., removing boilerplate, special characters, URLs, and emails).
* Implemented a full preprocessing pipeline method to combine filtering, cleaning, and removal of empty records, with logging at each step for transparency and traceability.
* Added utility methods to save the preprocessed data to CSV and retrieve the processed DataFrame.

author: yairfalse
body:
## Summary
- Delete `Executor.Behaviour` and `Executor.Local` (redundant parallel interface)
- Add `Target.Local.run_task_stateless/2` for stateless RPC dispatch
- Rewrite `Executor.Mesh` to implement `Target.Behaviour` with state composition

## Why
Before this PR, there were two parallel interfaces for execution:
- `Target.Behaviour` - state-based lifecycle (setup → run → teardown)
- `Executor.Behaviour` - stateless execution

This consolidates around a single `Target.Behaviour` interface. The `run_task_stateless/2` function enables RPC dispatch where callers can't manage state.

## Changes
- **-541 lines**: Removed `Executor.Behaviour` and `Executor.Local`
- **+37 lines**: Added `run_task_stateless/2` to `Target.Local`
- **Rewritten**: `Executor.Mesh` now implements `Target.Behaviour`

## Test plan
- [x] All 531 tests pass
- [x] Mesh tests updated for new Target interface
- [x] Added tests for `run_task_stateless/2`

body:
### Motivation
- Keep `run_full_system_selftest()` as an always-pass, torch-free smoke test and avoid embedding failing negative cases in it.
- Provide a separate entrypoint that executes deliberate contract violations to validate enforcement behavior.
- Ensure adoption/quarantine constraints and critic-approved adoption semantics are tested by behavior rather than only by flags in `gap_spec`.
- Make negative checks explicit so expected failures are asserted and unexpected exceptions are not silenced.

### Description
- Add `run_contract_negative_tests()` which instantiates an `Orchestrator`, runs `run_recursive_cycle()`, and performs positive schema asserts plus multiple deliberate negative tests.
- Implement an `expect_failure()` helper that verifies a callable raises the expected exception types (e.g., `AssertionError`, `KeyError`).
- Add negative test cases for bad adoption logic, missing payload keys (`candidate`, `verdict`, `quarantine_only`, `gid`, `approval_key`), and an adopt-without-verdict case invoking `orch._adopt_proposal()`.
- Preserve `run_full_system_selftest()` as the torch-free always-pass self-test that still prints the three verification messages.

### Testing
- Ran `python -c "import NON_RSI_AGI_CORE_v5 as core; core.run_full_system_selftest()"` which exited with code 0 and printed `recursive rule loop executed`, `critic decision received`, and `tensor execution verified (torch-free)`.
- Ran `python -c "import NON_RSI_AGI_CORE_v5 as core; core.run_contract_negative_tests()"` which exited with code 0 and produced no stdout, indicating the negative checks triggered the expected exceptions without unexpected failures.
- Automated test status: both commands completed successfully (exit code 0).
- No additional automated test failures were observed.

Adds unit tests, instrumented UI tests, and GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline to validate ANR detection, memory leak detection, and app functionality.

## Test Coverage

**Unit Tests** (9 tests)
- `ANRWatchdogTest.kt`: Tests singleton pattern, fluent API, start/stop behavior, and timeout configuration

**Instrumented Tests** (20 tests)
- `MainActivityTest.kt`: UI interactions, tab switching, button states
- `AnrSimulationTest.kt`: Main thread blocking detection, stack trace capture, duration validation
- `FloatingDebugViewTest.kt`: Active thread collection, memory/CPU metrics, state persistence
- `MemoryLeakTest.kt`: LeakCanary integration, lifecycle leak detection across activities and fragments

## CI/CD Pipeline

**Workflow**: `.github/workflows/android-ci.yml`
- **test**: Executes unit tests via `./gradlew test`
- **build**: Compiles debug APK and uploads artifact
- **instrumented-test**: Runs UI tests on Android emulator (API 29, x86_64)

Triggers on push to `main`, `develop`, `copilot/**` and PRs to `main`, `develop`.

dependencies {

    testImplementation("org.mockito:mockito-core:5.3.1")

### Motivation
- Provide a way to export and import the entire app state stored in `localStorage` so users can share data across devices.
- Include a single file containing all `localStorage` keys (turnos, configuración, equipos, etc.) to simplify transfers.
- Warn users that importing will replace all existing local data to avoid accidental data loss.
- Prefer a spreadsheet format was suggested but a JSON backup was chosen as the most reliable format for full localStorage export/import.

### Description
- Added an `Exportar e importar` section to the end of the Setup page in `src/pages/SetupPage.tsx` and wired UI buttons for export and import.
- Implemented `handleExportData` which collects all `localStorage` entries into a payload (`{ version, exportedAt, items }`) and downloads it as a JSON file.
- Implemented `handleImportData` with an `input` file chooser (referenced by `importInputRef`) that confirms overwrite, parses the JSON (supports payloads with an `items` object or a flat map), clears `localStorage`, writes entries back, and reloads the app.
- Added `handleImportClick` to trigger the hidden file input and basic input validation to ensure a single JSON file is processed.

### Testing
- Started the dev server with `npm run dev` and confirmed the app served at the local URL; this succeeded.
- Executed an automated Playwright script that opened the app, navigated to `Configuración`, scrolled and captured a screenshot of the new section; the script completed successfully and produced a screenshot.
- No unit test suite changes were added or executed for this UI feature.
- Verified the code compiled and the change was committed to the repository successfully.

author: joepentony-dot
body:
### Motivation
- Desktop scroll passthrough was previously enabled by making decorative overlay layers non-interactive, but that change also blocked clicks on Home featured YouTube videos. 
- The intent is a minimal CSS-only fix to restore click/tap for the featured videos without reverting the desktop scroll passthrough or altering visuals or layout. 

### Description
- Re-enabled interaction for featured video elements by adding `pointer-events: auto` to ` .home-video-card`, `.home-video-card__media`, `.home-featured-video-media`, `.home-video-card__iframe`, and `.home-video-card__play` in `resources/css/home.css`.
- Added small `z-index` bumps on video elements (`z-index: 2`/`3`/`4` as appropriate) so video controls and iframes sit above decorative overlays while preserving visible stacking and appearance. 
- Kept the desktop-only overlay passthrough (`pointer-events: none`) for decorative layers intact in the overlay rules so scrolling behavior is not changed. 
- Changes are narrowly scoped to Home featured video selectors inside `resources/css/home.css` to avoid re-enabling pointer events site-wide. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

Implements automatic container restart on system reboot with proper
dependency ordering and health monitoring.

Changes:
- Enable podman.socket and podman-restart.service for boot persistence
- Add health checks to all containers (PostgreSQL, Redis, Quay, Clair)
- Configure container dependencies (Quay requires PostgreSQL/Redis,
  Clair requires PostgreSQL, Mirror requires all services)
- Generate systemd unit files for each container with proper ordering
- Add comprehensive documentation on restart persistence features
- Include testing procedures for verifying restart persistence

This ensures the POC environment survives system reboots and containers
start in the correct order with health verification.

body:
Addresses code review feedback from PR #40 regarding PEP 8 compliance and PyTorch API usage.

## Changes

- **flow_trainer.py**: Replace `torch.cuda.amp.autocast` with `torch.autocast` for device-agnostic mixed precision support. Extracts device type from string format (`'cuda:0'` → `'cuda'`) to properly set autocast parameters.

- **version.py**, **visualization.py**, **era5.py**: Move inline imports (`re`, `warnings`, `pathlib.Path`) to module level per PEP 8.

```python
# Before
with torch.cuda.amp.autocast(enabled=self.use_amp, device_type='cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'):
    ...

# After  
device_type = str(self.device).split(':')[0]
with torch.autocast(
    device_type=device_type if device_type in ("cuda", "cpu") else "cpu",
    enabled=self.use_amp and device_type == "cuda",
):
    ...
```

author: llsenyue
body:
## Overview / 概述

This PR introduces **Smart Warmup** to help users proactively trigger Gemini API's 5-hour quota recovery cycle, solving the "full quota but unusable" problem. It also enhances the API monitoring dashboard and response headers.

本 PR 引入了**智能预热机制 (Smart Warmup)**，帮助用户主动触发 Gemini API 的 5 小时配额恢复周期，彻底解决"配额满值但无法使用"的问题。同时优化了 API 监控看板和响应头信息。

---

## 🔥 Core Feature: Smart Warmup / 核心功能：智能预热

### Why Warmup? / 为什么需要预热？

Gemini Pro/Ultra accounts follow a **5-hour recovery cycle**:  
Gemini Pro/Ultra 账号遵循 **5 小时恢复周期**：

- After usage, quota enters cooldown and recovers after 5 hours  
  配额在使用后进入冷却期，5 小时后自动恢复
- **Problem**: Unused accounts stay at 100% but haven't started recovery  
  **问题**：长时间未使用的账号配额保持在 100%，但并未进入恢复周期
- **Result**: Quota is consumed immediately when needed, requiring 5h wait  
  **结果**：真正使用时配额立即消耗，需等待 5 小时恢复

**Warmup**: Sends minimal request (~1 token) to trigger recovery cycle proactively.  
**预热**：发送极小请求（~1 token），主动触发配额恢复周期。

### Smart Warmup Features / 智能预热特性

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Quota-aware** | Only warms up models at 100%, skips <100% (already in cooldown) |
| **Minimal consumption** | Text: `maxOutputTokens=1`, Image: `TEXT` mode |
| **Per-account warmup** | New warmup button in account action column |
| **Auto-refresh** | Automatically refreshes quotas 5 seconds after warmup |

| 特性 | 描述 |
|------|------|
| **配额感知** | 只预热 100% 的模型，<100% 自动跳过（已在冷却期） |
| **最小消耗** | 文本模型用 `maxOutputTokens=1`，图片模型用 `TEXT` 模式 |
| **单账号预热** | 在账号操作列新增预热按钮 |
| **自动刷新** | 预热完成 5 秒后自动刷新配额显示 |

### Usage / 使用方式

1. **One-click warmup**: Click "Warm Up" button in accounts toolbar  
   **一键预热**：点击账号页面顶部工具栏的"一键预热"按钮
2. **Per-account warmup**: Click warmup icon ⚡ in account action column  
   **单账号预热**：在目标账号操作列点击预热图标 ⚡

---

## 📊 API Monitor Enhancements / API 监控增强

- **Account filter**: Filter requests by account email  
  **账号筛选器**：支持按邮箱筛选请求日志
- **Fixed log loss**: Fixed SQL query missing `mapped_model` column  
  **修复日志丢失**：修复 SQL 查询缺失 `mapped_model` 列的问题
- **Fixed filter logic**: Fixed Gemini/error filter conditions  
  **修复筛选逻辑**：修复 Gemini/错误筛选条件判断

---

## 🏷️ Response Headers / 响应头增强

| Header | Description | 描述 |
|--------|-------------|------|
| `X-Account-Email` | Shows account email used | 显示使用的账号邮箱 |
| `X-Mapped-Model` | Shows actual mapped model ID | 显示实际映射的模型 ID |

---

## ❄️ Cooldown Indicator / 冷却指示器

Shows ❄️ emoji for models with quota <100% in account list.  
在账号列表中使用 ❄️ emoji 标识配额 <100% 的模型冷却状态。

---

## 📁 Files Changed / 文件变更

- **28 files**, +2062 lines, -1041 lines
- Core: [quota.rs](cci:7://file:///f:/backup/home/llsenyue/project/Antigravity-Manager-Doctor/src-tauri/src/modules/quota.rs:0:0-0:0), `scheduler.rs`, [ProxyMonitor.tsx](cci:7://file:///f:/backup/home/llsenyue/project/Antigravity-Manager-Doctor/src/components/proxy/ProxyMonitor.tsx:0:0-0:0), `Settings.tsx`
- Handlers: `gemini.rs`, `claude.rs`, [openai.rs](cci:7://file:///f:/backup/home/llsenyue/project/Antigravity-Manager-Doctor/src-tauri/src/proxy/handlers/openai.rs:0:0-0:0) (X-Account-Email header)
- i18n: [zh.json](cci:7://file:///f:/backup/home/llsenyue/project/Antigravity-Manager-Doctor/src/locales/zh.json:0:0-0:0), `en.json`

body:
The plugin already supports Facebook Business Login (Instagram, Pages, business management) through the existing Facebook SDK integration. Users just needed documentation showing how to request business permissions.

## Changes

**Documentation**
- Added `docs/facebook_business_login.md` (386 lines) - complete setup guide covering business app configuration, permission reference, App Review process, platform-specific notes, and troubleshooting
- Enhanced README with Facebook Business Login section showing Instagram and Pages examples
- Created `docs/examples/facebook_business_login_examples.ts` (405 lines) - 10 working examples for common business integration patterns

**TypeScript Definitions**
- Enhanced `FacebookLoginOptions.permissions` JSDoc with comprehensive business permission reference (Instagram, Pages, Business assets)
- Added documentation links and usage examples

## Usage

```typescript
// Instagram Basic Display
const result = await SocialLogin.login({
  provider: 'facebook',
  options: {
    permissions: ['email', 'instagram_basic', 'pages_show_list']
  }
});

// Fetch Instagram account via Graph API
const profile = await SocialLogin.providerSpecificCall({
  call: 'facebook#getProfile',
  options: {
    fields: ['instagram_business_account{id,username,followers_count}']
  }
});
```

**Supported business permissions now documented**: `instagram_basic`, `instagram_manage_insights`, `pages_show_list`, `pages_manage_posts`, `business_management`, and 20+ more.

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive warnings-as-errors enforcement across the entire development toolchain to maintain code quality and prevent warning fatigue.

### Changes Included

**1. Fixed All act() Warnings (13 commits)**
- Fixed 4 warnings in Popover.test.tsx by wrapping RAF waits in act()
- Fixed 2 warnings in Avatar.test.tsx
- Fixed 6 warnings in Tree.test.tsx  
- Fixed 2 warnings in Tooltip.test.tsx through refactoring
- All 57 test files now pass with zero warnings

**2. Lint Strict Mode**
- Added `--max-warnings 0` flag to lint script
- ESLint now fails on ANY warning

**3. Test Strict Mode**
- Created `scripts/test-strict.sh` wrapper script
- Detects act() warnings, console.warn, console.error patterns
- Updated `test:ci` to use strict wrapper

**4. Build Strict Mode**
- Created `scripts/build-strict.sh` wrapper script
- Detects TypeScript warnings (`warning TS`, `⚠`)
- Updated build script to use strict wrapper

**5. Pre-push Hook**
- Installed Husky v9.1.7
- Created `.husky/pre-push` hook
- Runs typecheck → lint → test:ci before allowing push
- Blocks push if any warnings detected

**6. CI Workflows**
- Updated `.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml`
- Added clarifying comments for strict mode enforcement
- Test job now uses `test:ci` (strict wrapper)

**7. Documentation**
- Added "Warnings Policy" section to CLAUDE.md
- Documented zero-tolerance approach and rationale
- Added note to Development Commands section

### Test Results

- ✅ All 57 test files passing (922 tests)
- ✅ Zero warnings across entire test suite
- ✅ All enforcement layers verified working:
  - Local development (npm scripts)
  - Pre-push protection (git hooks)  
  - CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions)
  - Publish protection (prepublishOnly)

### Breaking Changes

None for end users. Developers will now have stricter quality gates that fail on any warnings.

### Migration Notes

After merging, all developers should:
1. Run `npm install` to get Husky hooks
2. Ensure their code has zero lint/test/build warnings
3. Pre-push hook will automatically enforce this going forward

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## 功能需求：AI 模型集成

实现 AI 模型集成功能，支持 OpenAI 和 DeepSeek 两种 API，用于后续的智能命令识别。

### 核心功能

1. **AI 提供商抽象层**
   - 创建统一的 AI 接口
   - 支持 OpenAI API
   - 支持 DeepSeek API（兼容 OpenAI SDK 格式）
   - 可灵活切换不同的 AI 提供商

2. **配置管理**
   - 使用 `.env` 文件管理 API 密钥（安全）
   - 支持以下配置项：
     ```
     AI_PROVIDER=deepseek          # 或 openai
     OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-xxx
     OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
     OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4
     
     DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-xxx
     DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/v1
     DEEPSEEK_MODEL=deepseek-chat
     ```
   - 提供 `.env.example` 示例文件
   - 更新 `.gitignore` 忽略 `.env` 文件

3. **AI 调用功能**
   - 封装统一的 `generate_response()` 方法
   - 支持系统提示词（system prompt）
   - 支持用户消息
   - 支持对话历史
   - 错误处理（API 错误、网络错误、超时等）
   - 返回 AI 生成的文本内容

### 技术实现

**新建文件：`ai_provider.py`**

```python
"""
AI 提供商抽象层
支持 OpenAI 和 DeepSeek API
"""
import os
from typing import List, Dict, Optional
from openai import OpenAI
from dotenv import load_dotenv

class AIProvider:
    """AI 提供商基类"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        load_dotenv()
        self.provider = os.getenv("AI_PROVIDER", "deepseek").lower()
        self.client = self._init_client()
    
    def _init_client(self) -> OpenAI:
        """初始化 AI 客户端"""
        if self.provider == "openai":
            return OpenAI(
                api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
                base_url=os.getenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1")
            )
        elif self.provider == "deepseek":
            return OpenAI(
                api_key=os.getenv("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"),
                base_url=os.getenv("DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL", "https://api.deepseek.com/v1")
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"不支持的 AI 提供商: {self.provider}")
    
    def get_model(self) -> str:
        """获取当前使用的模型"""
        if self.provider == "openai":
            return os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4")
        elif self.provider == "deepseek":
            return os.getenv("DEEPSEEK_MODEL", "deepseek-chat")
    
    def generate_response(
        self,
        system_prompt: str,
        user_message: str,
        history: Optional[List[Dict[str, str]]] = None,
        temperature: float = 0.7,
        max_tokens: int = 1000
    ) -> str:
        """
        生成 AI 响应
        
        Args:
            system_prompt: 系统提示词
            user_message: 用户消息
            history: 对话历史 [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}, ...]
            temperature: 温度参数（0-1）
            max_tokens: 最大 token 数
            
        Returns:
            AI 生成的文本响应
        """
        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}]
        
        if history:
            messages.extend(history)
        
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
        
        try:
            response = self.client.chat.completions.create(
                model=self.get_model(),
                messages=messages,
                temperature=temperature,
                max_tokens=max_tokens
            )
            return response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
        except Exception as e:
            raise Exception(f"AI 调用失败: {str(e)}")
```

**创建 `.env.example` 文件：**

```bash
# AI 提供商配置（选择 openai 或 deepseek）
AI_PROVIDER=deepseek

# OpenAI 配置
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-openai-api-key-here
OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4

# DeepSeek 配置
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-your-deepseek-api-key-here
DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/v1
DEEPSEEK_MODEL=deepseek-chat
```

**更新 `.gitignore`：**

添加以下内容：
```

```

**更新 `requirements.txt`：**

添加以下依赖：
```
openai>=1.0.0
python-dotenv>=1.0.0
```

**创建测试文件：`test_ai_provider.py`**

```python
"""测试 AI 提供商"""
from ai_provider import AIProvider

def test_ai_provider():
    """测试 AI 调用"""
    try:
        ai = AIProvider()
        print(f"✓ 使用 AI 提供商: {ai.provider}")
        print(f"✓ 使用模型: {ai.get_model()}")
        
        # 测试简单调用
        response = ai.generate_response(
            system_prompt="你是一个 Linux 命令助手。",
            user_message="将'列出所有文件'转换为 Linux 命令，只返回命令本身，不要解释。"
        )
        print(f"✓ AI 响应: {response}")
        print("\n✅ AI 模型集成测试成功！")
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ 错误: {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_ai_provider()
```

# 📦 Gestão de Conciliações de Inventário

## 📚 Histórias Atendidas

### 🟦 História 136675 --- Gerenciamento de Conciliações

Foi implementado no sistema o menu **Inventário**,  contendo o sub-menu **Gerenciamento
de Conciliações**.

Ao acessar essa funcionalidade, o usuário passa a visualizar a listagem
de conciliações com as seguintes informações:

-   **Unidade Administrativa**: Código e Nome\
-   **Status da UA**: Ativa ou Inativa\
-   **Número de Bens**: Quantidade de bens vinculados à UA\
-   **Vigência**: Ano de vigência da conciliação (ex.: 2025)\
-   **Tipo**: Eventual ou Anual\
-   **Número da Conciliação**\
-   **Status da Conciliação**:
    -   Em aberto\
    -   Fechado\
    -   Fechado pelo Administrador\
-   **Ações**: botão para visualizar detalhes da conciliação

#### 🔍 Filtros Disponíveis

-   **Busca geral** (topo): Número da Conciliação ou Unidade
    Administrativa\
-   **Filtro lateral por Vigência**: seleção de ano\
-   **Filtro lateral por Status da Conciliação**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 🟦 História 140172 --- Conciliação Anual Automática

O sistema passou a controlar automaticamente o ciclo da **Conciliação
Anual**, conforme regras abaixo:

-   A conciliação anual é **aberta automaticamente em 01/01**
-   O período padrão de encerramento é **31/03**
-   O Gestor de Patrimônio pode configurar datas personalizadas por meio
    do **Parâmetro de Conciliação Anual**
-   Caso encerrada automaticamente pelo sistema, a conciliação recebe o
    status:\
    **Fechado pelo Administrador -- Não Conciliado**

#### ⚙️ Regras de Funcionamento

-   A conciliação anual é criada apenas se:
    -   A Unidade Administrativa estiver **ativa**
    -   A Unidade possuir **ao menos um bem patrimonial**
    -   Não existir conciliação anual para o mesmo ano de referência
-   Caso exista conciliação eventual em aberto para o mesmo ano:
    -   Ela é **fechada automaticamente** antes da criação da anual
-   Após o término do período permitido:
    -   Conciliações anuais ainda abertas são **fechadas automaticamente
        pelo sistema**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🧠 Regras de Negócio Implementadas

-   Uma Unidade Administrativa pode possuir:
    -   Apenas **uma conciliação anual por ano de referência**
-   Conciliações anuais:
    -   Podem existir como **Em aberto** ou **Fechadas**
    -   Nunca são recriadas para o mesmo período
-   Gestor de Patrimônio:
    -   Pode criar conciliações para **todas as Unidades Administrativas
        ativas**
    -   Caso esteja vinculado a uma UA específica, o processamento se
        restringe a ela
-   Usuários não gestores:
    -   Processam conciliações apenas da UA vinculada ao seu perfil

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 🧪 Testes Automatizados

Foram adicionados testes unitários para garantir a consistência da
conciliação automática:

-   ✅ Não cria conciliação se a Unidade não possuir bens
-   ✅ Cria conciliação anual automaticamente dentro do período válido
-   ✅ Respeita parametrização de período por ano de referência
-   ✅ Não duplica conciliações anuais
-   ✅ Fecha conciliações eventuais abertas automaticamente

Execução dos testes:

``` bash
docker compose exec web python manage.py test inventario.tests.test_conciliacao_automatica -v 2
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 📊 Impacto no Sistema

-   Nenhuma quebra de compatibilidade
-   Conciliações existentes permanecem válidas
-   Lógica de criação automática centralizada e segura
-   Regras de domínio reforçadas com testes automatizados

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ✅ Checklist

-   [x] Menu e listagem implementados\
-   [x] Filtros funcionais\
-   [x] Conciliação anual automática\
-   [x] Parametrização por período\
-   [x] Regras de unicidade garantidas\
-   [x] Testes automatizados adicionados

------------------------------------------------------------------------

🚀 **Funcionalidade pronta para uso e validada por testes
automatizados**

Configures all LLM providers (Mistral, Gemini, Ollama, Azure) to work via Meilisearch's chat interface.

Changes:
- Updated ChatWorkspaceSettings to include org_id, project_id, and correct source mapping.
- Implemented specific configure_for_chat logic for Gemini and Ollama.
- Fixed main.rs to poll for Meilisearch health instead of sleeping.
- Fixed frontend compilation error in chat/mod.rs regarding Send trait compliance.

Fixes # (if applicable)

## Summary by Sourcery

Configure Meilisearch-based chat streaming across LLM providers and improve frontend/TAURI integration.

New Features:
- Add Meilisearch chat streaming support that routes stream_chat through the Meilisearch chat manager instead of the legacy router.
- Introduce a chat_stream_with_history API on the Meilisearch chat manager for streaming responses with conversation history.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix Meilisearch chat client initialization by polling sidecar health and configuring the chat client on startup instead of relying on sleep.
- Resolve frontend Send/Sync issues in the chat component by restructuring the streaming listener setup for WASM.
- Fix TAURI invoke bindings to correctly propagate JS-side errors via the invoke_raw catch mechanism.
- Correct Meilisearch index settings update to use the chatCompletions flag instead of the deprecated chat flag.
- Fix various frontend warnings and type issues, including unused variables, event argument types, and Blob options usage.

Enhancements:
- Extend ChatWorkspaceSettings to support Azure-style deployment, API version, organization, and project IDs, and align Meilisearch chat settings with provider configurations for OpenAI, Mistral, Gemini, Ollama, and Azure OpenAI.
- Refactor chat provider configuration mapping to Meilisearch workspace settings, including proper vLLM/Ollama base URLs and placeholder auth where required.
- Convert the design-system Button component to accept reactive MaybeSignal flags for disabled and loading, simplifying its use with Leptos signals.
- Improve analytics and settings components to rely on reactive loading signals instead of manually reading values, and clean up unused parameters in graph components.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure a stop-loss is always established before take-profit so filled buys show the loss condition and are protected (`placeExitOrders`).
- Avoid showing trades the user cannot close by hiding rows for pairs with zero base-asset available balance.
- Provide a per-pair view of open orders and automatically remove stale trade records when no open orders remain (`GET /api/orders/open`).
- Prevent redundant or failing force-close attempts by detecting already-filled exit orders and verifying base balance prior to placing a market sell (`POST /api/order/close`).

### Description
- Reordered logic in `placeExitOrders` to place the stop-loss before the take-profit and wrapped TP placement in a `try/catch` to update the trade `message` on TP failure.
- Added `findBalanceForAsset` and expanded `getPairMeta` to include `base`/`quote`, and used these in `POST /api/order/close` to detect filled exit orders and verify available base balance before placing a market sell.
- Implemented `GET /api/orders/open` that normalizes pair names, returns matching open orders and deletes the `trades` DB row when no open orders remain, and updated `account.html` to fetch pair metadata/prices, hide trades with no base balance, add an `Open Orders` modal triggered by a `View` button, and remove rows client-side when the API reports deletion.
- Unified quick-profit sizing by adding `QUICK_PROFIT_PCT`, `KRAKEN_FEE_PCT`, and `targetMovePct()` and applying them in `server.js`, `cron_alerts.js`, and `strategy.html`, and accepted `cron_key` as a query fallback for the cron endpoint.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for these changes.
- No CI/test run was performed as part of this update.

body:
## Summary
- Prevents users from setting `is_admin=true` or `is_approved=true` when creating their profile
- Moves admin email list from client-side code to database (hidden from clients)
- Adds database trigger to auto-promote admin emails server-side

## Security Issue (Critical)
The RLS INSERT policy only checked `auth.uid() = id`, allowing any user to self-promote to admin by calling:
```js
supabase.from('profiles').insert({ id: uid, is_admin: true, is_approved: true })
```

## Changes
- [009_fix_profile_self_promotion.sql](scripts/009_fix_profile_self_promotion.sql): New migration with secure policy + trigger
- [signup/page.tsx](app/src/app/auth/signup/page.tsx): Remove client-side admin check
- [callback/route.ts](app/src/app/auth/callback/route.ts): Remove client-side admin check  
- [types.ts](app/src/lib/types.ts): Remove `ADMIN_EMAILS` constant from client bundle
- [notify-signup/route.ts](app/src/app/api/admin/notify-signup/route.ts): Fetch admin emails from DB

## Deployment Steps
1. Run `scripts/009_fix_profile_self_promotion.sql` in Supabase SQL Editor
2. Deploy updated app

## Test plan
- [ ] New admin email signup gets auto-approved via trigger

body:
### Motivation

- Prevent overflow/NaN and Newton/substepping hangs caused by inconsistent void-element penalization in bulk assembly.
- Ensure empty/void elements still produce a finite (non-zero) reaction for the Case 01 pullout example.
- Make bond-layer assembly robust when legacy (single-layer) bond state is provided while multi-layer layers are configured.
- Add a CLI regression that explicitly captures the Case 01 non-zero reaction and forbids numeric matmul/overflow warnings.

### Description

- In `assemble_xfem_system` introduced a `bulk_scale` (set to `1e-6` for void elements) and use `sig_use = sig * bulk_scale` and `Ct_scaled = Ct * bulk_scale` so both stresses and tangent are consistently penalized, and used `fe = B.T @ sig_use * weight` and `Ke = (B.T @ Ct_scaled @ B) * weight` to avoid mismatched scaling.
- For void elements, keep a finite thickness (use global `thickness` or `1.0` fallback) to avoid double extreme penalization and singular thickness cases while making penalization come primarily from `bulk_scale`.
- Add a fallback in bond-layer assembly to convert a legacy single `bond_states_comm` into a `[bond_states_comm, None, ...]` list when `bond_layers` is used so each explicit layer has an associated state entry.
- Update the slow CLI regression test `tests/test_case01_pullout_cli.py` to run a single step (`--nsteps 1`), set `PYTHONPATH` so the CLI runs in tests, allow the single expected "Ambiguous bond-slip units" warning once, assert no numeric `matmul`/`overflow` warnings from `assembly_single.py`, and require the reported reaction `P` to be non-zero (`|P| > 1e-6 kN`).

### Testing

- Ran the CLI: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m examples.gutierrez_thesis.run --case 01_pullout_lettow --mesh coarse --nsteps 1 --no-post --no-numba --output-dir /tmp/case01_debug2`, which completed in ~0.7s, emitted no numeric matmul/overflow warnings from `assembly_single.py`, and produced a non-zero reaction (`P` reported).
- Executed the updated pytest regression for the case: `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest -q --runslow -k case01`, and the Case 01 CLI test passed (1 passed, 1 skipped for the run target).
- The updated test allows the single expected bond-slip unit warning only once (`Ambiguous bond-slip units`) and fails if numeric `overflow`/`invalid value` messages appear.
- The changes are limited in scope to `src/xfem_clean/xfem/assembly_single.py` and the Case 01 CLI test `tests/test_case01_pullout_cli.py`.

author: johncari
body:
## Summary

This PR implements automatic reconnection handling for PostgreSQL replication connections, addressing issue #10.

**Key changes:**
- Add `is_connection_retryable()` method to `ErrorKind` for classifying transient vs permanent errors
- Add `ReconnectionConfig` struct with configurable retry parameters (initial delay, max delay, backoff multiplier, max duration)
- Add `ReconnectionManager` with exponential backoff and jitter to prevent thundering herd
- Add `reconnection_loop` wrapper that automatically reconnects on transient failures
- Integrate reconnection into `ApplyWorker::start()` when enabled via configuration

**Reconnection behavior:**
- Retryable errors: `SourceConnectionFailed`, `SourceIoError`, `SourceDatabaseShutdown`, `SourceDatabaseInRecovery`, `IoError`
- Non-retryable errors (immediate failure): `AuthenticationError`, `PermissionDenied`, `ConfigError`, etc.
- Exponential backoff with 30% jitter to distribute retry attempts
- Configurable max retry duration (default: 5 minutes) before giving up
- Comprehensive logging at each stage (connection lost, retry attempt, reconnection success/failure)

**Configuration defaults:**
```rust
ReconnectionConfig {
    enabled: false,  // Opt-in for backward compatibility
    initial_retry_delay_ms: 1000,
    max_retry_delay_ms: 30000,
    backoff_multiplier: 2.0,
    max_retry_duration_ms: 300000,  // 5 minutes
}
```

Closes #10

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for `ReconnectionManager` (backoff calculation, retry logic, state transitions)
- [x] Unit tests for `ReconnectionState` (failure recording, success reset)
- [x] `cargo test` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy` passes with no warnings
- [ ] Manual testing with simulated network interruption (requires live database)
- [ ] Integration test for reconnection scenarios (optional, marked in tasks.md)

author: copilot
body:
Adds UI for managing user-application permissions (READ/WRITE/ADMIN) through the BFF service. Users can select any user and modify permissions for all applications in a single batch operation.

## Architecture

**PermissionService** (`core/services/permission.service.ts`)
- Wraps BFF permission endpoints (`/api/applications`, `/api/users/{id}/permissions`, `/api/permissions`)
- `batchUpdatePermissions()` analyzes delta between current and desired state, executes minimal create/update/delete operations via `forkJoin`
- Permission levels hardcoded temporarily (TODO: add backend endpoint)

**PermissionMatrixComponent** (`features/permissions/components/permission-matrix/`)
- Matrix UI: rows = applications, columns = permission levels + none
- Radio button groups per application ensure single selection
- On save: builds permission map, service determines diff, parallel API calls execute
- Reloads permissions post-save to sync with backend state (audit logs, timestamps)

## Implementation

```typescript
// Intelligent batch update - only touches what changed
batchUpdatePermissions(userId: number, matrix: PermissionMatrix): Observable<any> {
  return this.getUserPermissions(userId).pipe(
    switchMap(existing => {
      const ops: Observable<any>[] = [];
      const existingMap = new Map(existing.map(p => [p.application.id, p]));
      
      matrix.permissions.forEach(desired => {
        const current = existingMap.get(desired.applicationId);
        if (desired.permissionLevelId === null && current) {
          ops.push(this.deletePermission(current.id));
        } else if (current && current.permissionLevel.id !== desired.permissionLevelId) {
          ops.push(this.updatePermission(current.id, {permissionLevelId: desired.permissionLevelId}));
        } else if (!current && desired.permissionLevelId !== null) {
          ops.push(this.createPermission({userId, ...desired}));
        }
      });
      
      return ops.length ? forkJoin(ops) : of([]);
    })
  );
}
```

## UI Structure

- User dropdown → permission matrix loads current state
- Dynamic column headers from `permissionLevels` array (no hardcoded IDs)
- Single "一括保存" button for atomic updates
- Route: `/permissions` (AuthGuard protected)
- Navigation link added to app header

## Technical Notes

- Uses `??` for null-safety over `||` to handle falsy permission level 0
- Template uses `*ngFor` over permission levels for maintainability
- No manual state sync - permissions reload after save ensures consistency

body:
## Summary
- Changes `get_patterns_by_keywords` from SECURITY DEFINER to SECURITY INVOKER
- Revokes `anon` execute permission on database functions
- Adds explicit approval check as defense-in-depth

## Security Issue (Critical)
`get_patterns_by_keywords` used `SECURITY DEFINER` and granted execute to `anon` role. This allowed unauthenticated users to query all pattern data by calling:
```sql
SELECT * FROM get_patterns_by_keywords(ARRAY[1,2,3], 0, 1000, NULL)
```
This completely bypassed RLS since SECURITY DEFINER runs with owner privileges.

## Changes
- [010_fix_security_definer_bypass.sql](scripts/010_fix_security_definer_bypass.sql): Migration to fix both functions

## Deployment Steps
Run `scripts/010_fix_security_definer_bypass.sql` in Supabase SQL Editor.

## Test plan
- [ ] Authenticated approved users can still filter by keywords
- [ ] Authenticated approved users can still use semantic search
- [ ] Unauthenticated API calls to these functions fail
- [ ] Unapproved users get "Access denied" error

author: lobotomy-x
body:
**Dump Key feature**

- off by default, can be set in the profile taking either a decimal or hex int value corresponding to VK scancode
- when enabled the startup process uses a detached thread to listen for keypresses, this has been streamlined from previous pr by using a lambda
- actual value of the key is printed to the console during config load which is helpful if the user has a local overriding profile and is generally just nice QOL
- requires std::thread and std::atomic to compile

**Sleep timeout feature**

- logic has been simplified and actually uses fewer conditionals either way
- when no dump key is set we just Sleep without bothering to check as the default value of 0 will yield the thread which effectively does nothing
- if we have a key setup then inside the same loop we do a shortcircuited eval that checks the elapsed time only if a sleep timeout 
- timeout is expected in ms as usual but when its less than 1000 we can assume the user probably wants it in seconds so we automatically convert that
- timeout settings are printed during config load just to clean up the main thread a little bit

**SDK path**

-  very minimal implementation, no environment variables or anything related to the dll file location in this patch
- If an absolute path is given it will work as expected, otherwise its relative to the game working dir and can use .. to access parent paths
 
The one change I see as possibly controversial is calling `using namespace std::chrono` in main thread. I did this to avoid having to wrap the short-circuited conditional that checks for the timeout and I also adjusted the final time calculation to use the same code and handle it inline with the print statement. If you prefer not to import the namespace or would rather use a shorthand as we already did for fs = filesystem in settings I can rewrite that. But its just an aesthetic change so if you don't mind it then I think we're good

I also did include a block of code that makes it so clicking and highlighting text on the console won't block the thread but I left it commented out in case thats an intended feature. I thought it made sense to leave it there for anyone compiling themselves since its not super well known and I personally find it annoying when I accidentally freeze a game. 

I did not bother with the example config and separate doc I had done earlier but I did add some basic explanation of features in the readme and anyone who builds it themselves should find adequate explanation in the comments as to why things are done the way they are. 

The detached thread inside the lambda is very well tested and isn't particularly fragile imo but if someone who has no clue what they're doing goes and tries to mess with that section they will probably have a bad time. e.g. if they want to capture another variable declared in the main thread, ignore the comment, and pass it by reference instead of by value it will 100% crash every time. So if you end up getting issues made about std::terminate or dangling reference crashes I would probably just tell them not to touch what they don't understand. I don't mind being tagged in an issue though and I'll add that if you wanted to ever update to C++ 20+ we can make it more thread safe with jthreads but I wasn't gonna push for that and I think this is totally fine as is.

body:
### Motivation
- Implement a synthetic training-data pipeline aligned to GSENet (arXiv:2303.07486v1) focusing on `y0`/`y1`/`yt` construction and the dB-domain sampling distributions in Table 1 / Section 2.1.
- Provide a small, dependency-light RIR generator so the pipeline is runnable without external room-acoustics libs.
- Make the pipeline testable and reproducible with unit tests and a runnable script that produces a sample `npz` batch. 

### Description
- Added gain utilities and sampling in `gsenet_repro/data/synthesis.py` including `db_to_amp`, `amp_to_db`, `sample_gains`, `Gains`, and the core `synthesize_pair` implementing the paper formulas for `y0`, `y1`, and `yt` (main-tap anechoic target extraction). 
- Implemented a simple, stable RIR generator `generate_dummy_rir` in `gsenet_repro/data/rir.py` that produces (3,2,L) RIRs and corresponding anechoic main-tap RIRs. 
- Added a runnable script `scripts/make_dummy_batch.py` that builds a batch of 8 examples, calls the generator/synthesizer, saves `artifacts/dummy_batch.npz` with `y0`, `y1`, `yt`, and `meta`, and prints a summary of `alpha_db`/`beta_db`/`pi` and a noise energy ratio. 
- Added unit tests in `tests/test_synthesis.py` covering truncation bounds, reproducibility, and deterministic contrast behavior, and a short README note describing how to run the script and the meaning of `y0`/`y1`/`yt`. 

### Testing
- Ran `python -m pytest -q` and the test suite passed: `4 passed in 1.59s`.
- Ran `python scripts/make_dummy_batch.py` and it generated `artifacts/dummy_batch.npz` and printed the summary line: `alpha_db(min/mean/max)=(-2.69/-0.82/3.49) beta_db(min/mean/max)=(4.00/5.10/12.31) pi_ratio=0.25 noise_ratio_mean=0.81`.
- An initial run of the dummy script failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gsenet_repro'`, which was resolved by adding the repository root to `sys.path` in the script so the script is now runnable as shown above.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a visible reference of role labels and their bytes32 hashes near the top of the actions panel so users can easily pick roles. 
- Ensure hashes remain aligned with `ethers.id()` by populating the reference dynamically rather than hardcoding values. 
- Surface the admin role and which roles are deployer roles (per contract `initialize()` / `_isDeployerRole`) to clarify access control. 
- Remind users that labels can be typed because `parseRole()` converts labels to hashes.

### Description
- Added a `.role-reference` section (table, styling, and note) to `IdentityRegistry.html` to display role information and the parsing note. 
- Introduced `ROLE_REFERENCE_ADMIN_LABEL` and `DEPLOYER_ROLE_LABELS` and implemented `renderRoleReference()` in `js/identityRegistry.js` to build the table from the existing `ROLE_LABELS`/`ROLE_HASHES`. 
- `renderRoleReference()` uses `ROLE_HASHES` and falls back to `ethers.id()` for the admin hash, and marks deployer flags `true` for `REGULATOR`, `ISSUER_STABLECOIN`, and `ISSUER_BOND`. 
- Called `renderRoleReference()` on `DOMContentLoaded` so the reference is populated when the page loads.

### Testing
- Launched a local static HTTP server and loaded `IdentityRegistry.html` via a Playwright script to capture a screenshot, and the page rendered the Role Reference section successfully. 
- No unit tests were added or run for these static UI changes.

author: jay-day
body:
This implementation moves netplay sync from plugin level to PIF RAM level, ensuring compatibility with all input plugins including raphnet.

Key changes:
- Added PIF sync callback system (pif_sync_callback.c/h)
- Implemented Kaillera API integration (Kaillera.cpp/hpp)
- Added controller detection emulation for remote players
- Removed obsolete plugin-level sync code from RMG-Input
- Added Kaillera session manager UI components

Technical details:
- Synchronization happens at update_pif_ram() after plugin processing
- Intercepts JCMD_STATUS/JCMD_RESET to force remote controllers as "present"
- Each player reads local controller from channel 0
- Synced inputs written to all channels (Player N → channel N-1)
- Works with raphnet, RMG-Input, and other input plugins

Fixes controller detection and input desync issues in Kaillera netplay.

author: tommy-raven
body:
### Motivation
- Enforce the invariant that files under `legacy_governance/deprecated/` and `legacy_governance/migration_sources/` include the required non-authoritative deprecation banner. 
- Provide a deterministic, reusable core for scanning legacy governance directories for missing banners. 
- Surface missing-banner cases as a first-class failure (`deprecation_violation`) that hard-fails promotion readiness. 

### Description
- Add `ai_cores/deprecation_core.py` which declares `REQUIRED_BANNER_LINES` and provides `find_deprecation_banner_violations()` to locate files missing the exact banner within the first 20 lines. 
- Add `scripts/deprecation_banner_validation.py` as a standalone validator that emits a `FailureLabel` with `Type: "deprecation_violation"` and `phase_id: "deprecation_banner_validation"` when a violation is found. 
- Extend `generator/failure_emitter.py` to recognize the `deprecation_violation` type and include an optional `path` field on `FailureLabel`, with corresponding validation and serialization. 
- Integrate the deprecation check into `scripts/run_promotion_readiness.py` so promotion gates fail fast when a missing banner is detected. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change. 
- The new modules and integrations were added and committed to the repository without running unit or integration test suites.

author: plexicus[bot]
body:
I replaced the vulnerable string-concatenated SQL statement with a parameterized query and bound parameters. Instead of building the SQL with f-strings (which allows an attacker to inject SQL by crafting username or password values), the code now uses a query with placeholders: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password = ?" and calls cursor.execute(query, (username, password)). This ensures the sqlite3 library treats the inputs as data, not executable SQL, eliminating SQL injection risk.

Additional notes and recommendations:
- Passwords: Never store or compare plaintext passwords. Use a secure password hashing algorithm (e.g., bcrypt, Argon2) and compare hashes instead of raw passwords.
- Error handling and resource management: Consider using context managers (with sqlite3.connect(db_file) as conn:) and try/except to ensure connections are closed and exceptions handled gracefully.
- Least privilege: Limit the database account permissions where possible.
- Logging: Avoid logging raw user input or sensitive data such as passwords.
- Constant-time comparison: For authentication flows, use safe comparison functions for hashed secrets to avoid timing attacks.

These changes address the immediate SQL injection weakness; applying the additional recommendations will further harden the authentication path.

Created by: letmein2@mailinator.com

body:
Eliminate redundant call to parse_all_files() in handle_emit_multi_file by using Option::take() to move ownership of the already-parsed program instead of parsing again.

Previously, when both AST emission and later stages (RIR, AIR, etc.) were requested, the code would clone ASTs from the parsed program, then re-parse all source files just to satisfy merge_symbols() ownership requirements. This wasted CPU time and memory.

Now, after cloning the ASTs for display, we use parsed.take() to transfer ownership to merge_symbols(), avoiding the redundant parsing.

Fixes rue-25tv

body:
## Purpose

This PR exposes the MLA prefill/decode batch split to `torch.compile`, enabling fusion opportunities for surrounding GEMMs and pointwise operations. This is **part 2/2** of the work to "lift the MLA prefill/decode split into the compiled region" tracked in #26516.

### Repro

```
VLLM_MLA_EXPOSED_SPLIT=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=True
```

### Changes

**New Custom Ops:**
- `mla_split_batch`: Returns `num_decode_tokens` as a data-dependent dynamic size (marked `cudagraph_unsafe`)
- `mla_attention_decode`: Wraps the decode attention kernel. Exposes W_UK_T and v_up_proj BMMs to torch.compile
- `mla_attention_prefill_with_output`: Wraps the prefill attention kernel. Exposes `kv_b_proj` to torch.compile

**New Forward Path:**
- Added `forward_exposed_split()` method to `MLAAttention` that exposes tensor slicing and GEMMs outside the custom ops
- Gated behind `VLLM_MLA_EXPOSED_SPLIT` environment variable (disabled by default)

**Configuration:**
- Added new ops to `_attention_ops` in `compilation.py` for piecewise cudagraph support


### Testing

Added `tests/compile/test_mla_exposed_split.py` with tests for correctness, piecewise cudagraph, and mixed batch scenarios.

cc @ProExpertProg 

---

> [!NOTE]
> <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) is generating a summary for commit c6037c3448dff738e0c706992229dc88ff8d7725. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).</sup>

---

> [!NOTE]
> Improves MLA compile-time fusion by lifting the prefill/decode split and surrounding GEMMs into the compiled region.
> 
> - Adds `VLLM_MLA_EXPOSED_SPLIT` path in `MLAAttention` (`forward_exposed_split`) that surfaces batch slicing and GEMMs to `torch.compile`
> - Introduces custom ops: `mla_split_batch` (dynamic split), `mla_attention_decode` (decode kernel wrapper), `mla_attention_prefill_with_output` (prefill kernel wrapper); registers them for piecewise cudagraphs
> - Refactors MLA layer/impl interfaces to support the exposed path (weight processing moved to layer, new prefill helpers, decode hook) and updates sparse backends to inherit the new common impl
> - Tweaks compilation settings to allow dynamic-shape captures and avoid graph breaks (Dynamo patches, backend interpreter change, wrapper config)
> - Updates attention op registry in `compilation.py`; adds env flag parsing in `envs.py`
> - Adds tests: compile-time MLA split correctness, cudagraph, mixed batches, inductor partition, and ensures custom ops registration; updates v1 MLA backend tests to instantiate real `MLAAttention` instead of mocks
>

body:
## Summary
Ensures Sentry events are flushed before the process exits, so we can see the actual crash reason.

## Why
Previous attempts showed the bot starting but crashing without any error in Sentry. This is because `process.exit(1)` was called immediately after `Sentry.captureException()`, not giving Sentry time to send the event.

## Changes
- Added `await Sentry.flush(5000)` before `process.exit(1)` in the `startBot().catch()` handler

author: copilot
body:
The `wthr.db` file contains weather caches and location search autocomplete data that should persist across package upgrades. Currently, RPM doesn't track this file, leading to undefined behavior during upgrades.

## Changes

- **Added `%ghost` directive** for `/var/lib/wthr/wthr.db` in the `%files` section
  - Tells RPM the file is owned by the package but created at runtime
  - Preserves file across upgrades and uninstalls

- **Hardened %post script** against symlink attacks
  - Check `! -L` before `! -e` to prevent symlink following
  - Use `install` command instead of `cp` + `chown` + `chmod` for atomic permissions

```diff
 %files
 %{_bindir}/wthr
 %{_unitdir}/wthr.service
 %{_datadir}/wthr
 %dir %attr(0750,wthr,wthr) %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr
+%ghost %attr(0640,wthr,wthr) %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr/wthr.db
```

```diff
 %post
 # Initialize DB from seed if missing
-if [ ! -f %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr/wthr.db ]; then
-    cp %{_datadir}/wthr/wthr.db.seed %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr/wthr.db
-    chown wthr:wthr %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr/wthr.db
-    chmod 640 %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr/wthr.db
+if [ ! -L %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr/wthr.db ] && [ ! -e %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr/wthr.db ]; then
+    install -m 0640 -o wthr -g wthr %{_datadir}/wthr/wthr.db.seed %{_sharedstatedir}/wthr/wthr.db
 fi
```

author: ricreig
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure the app persists the default UI/settings to the SQLite store so the map always boots with a stable centre/radius and user changes are saved. 
- Enforce feed filtering relative to the configured centre and radius to avoid showing aircraft outside the 250 NM area. 
- Provide bounded GeoJSON delivery and catalog metadata for better layer management and client-side `limit`/`bbox` support. 
- Detect and fail AIRAC/GeoJSON updates when generated GeoJSON contains out-of-range coordinates and surface richer diagnostics in `health.php`.

### Description
- Persist default settings on first GET in `api/settings.php` so the DB contains the default centre (MMZT 29.8839810 / -114.0747826), radius and other UI defaults, and keep the existing POST persistence behavior. 
- Recenter and filter feed results in `feed.php` by computing Haversine distance to the stored airport centre, rejecting aircraft with `distance_nm` > `radius`; store a rounded distance in `dst`/`distance_nm`. 
- Tighten feed status logic in the frontend (`index.php` client code) so the UI shows `OK` only when `error === null`, `cache_stale === false` and `upstream_http === 200`, otherwise show `DEGRADED` and surface an appropriate warning. 
- Extend `api/geojson.php` to accept a `limit` parameter (with sensible bounds), return `meta` (layer name, total features, returned, limit, truncated), and use `data/catalog.json` when present to report total feature counts. 
- Add GeoJSON validation integration to `update_airspace.php` by running `scripts/validate_geojson.php` after generation (function `runGeojsonValidation`) and fail on `out_of_range > 0`, additionally return `validation` details in the HTTP response; also persist `catalog.json` into `airspace.sqlite` (already supported). 
- Enhance `health.php` to report `cache_entries` and recent AIRAC runs (`recent_runs`) for richer diagnostics.

### Testing
- No automated test suite was executed for these changes (no CI/test runner invoked). 
- Changes were exercised locally by running the update/inspection workflow in the working tree (files modified: `api/settings.php`, `feed.php`, `index.php` (client JS), `api/geojson.php`, `update_airspace.php`, `health.php`). 
- The `scripts/validate_geojson.php` script is invoked by `update_airspace.php` and its stdout is parsed to detect `out_of_range` coordinate counts. 
- Manual verification steps are recommended: call `GET /api/settings.php`, call `GET /feed.php?lat=...&lon=...&radius_nm=...`, request a GeoJSON layer with `limit` and `bbox`, and run `php update_airspace.php <vatmex_path>` to observe validation output.

body:
New users see EDE's complexity (cells, metadata providers, execution engines) and wonder "Why not just use `Arrays.sort()`?" Without understanding the value proposition, they dismiss the framework before grasping its unique capabilities.

## Changes

Added **"Why Emergence?"** section between Overview and Quickstart with:

- **The Honest Trade-off** - Upfront: use `Arrays.sort()` for basic sorting. EDE trades efficiency for capabilities traditional algorithms lack.

- **Four Unique Capabilities** with working code examples:
  1. **Robustness on unreliable substrates** - frozen cells, fault tolerance
  2. **Emergent organization** - chimeric populations self-cluster by algotype
  3. **Observable delayed gratification** - monotonicity tracking shows temporary disorder

- **Decision criteria** - Clear ✅ use cases (research, observability, fault tolerance) and ❌ anti-patterns (performance-critical, production code).

    return new CellMetadata(algotype, SortDirection.ASCENDING);

<issue_description>## Problem

The EDE documentation explains *how* emergent computation works but never viscerally motivates *why* it matters. Without understanding the value proposition, users may dismiss the framework as over-engineered before grasping its unique capabilities.

## Solution

Add a "Why Emergence?" section to the main README that:
1. Acknowledges the complexity trade-off upfront
2. Explains unique capabilities traditional algorithms lack
3. Provides concrete use cases where emergence shines
4. Motivates the biological/morphogenesis inspiration

## Content Specification

### Section Structure

```markdown
## Why Emergence?

### The Honest Trade-off

If you just need to sort an array of integers, **use `Arrays.sort()`**. It's faster, simpler, and battle-tested.

The Emergent Doom Engine trades runtime efficiency for unique capabilities that traditional algorithms cannot provide:

### What Emergence Enables

#### 1. Robustness on Unreliable Substrates

Traditional sorting fails when parts of the array are locked or corrupted. EDE continues working:

```java
// Freeze 30% of array positions (simulate hardware defects)
frozenStatus.setFrozen(10, FrozenType.IMMOVABLE);
frozenStatus.setFrozen(25, FrozenType.IMMOVABLE);

// Sorting still converges around frozen cells!
engine.runUntilConvergence(5000);
```

**Real-world applications:**
- Fault-tolerant distributed systems
- Self-repairing data structures  
- Computation on degraded hardware

#### 2. Emergent Organization Patterns

Mix multiple sorting strategies in one array and watch spontaneous segregation emerge:

```java
// 50% bubble sort cells, 50% insertion sort cells (chimeric population)
IntFunction<CellMetadata> chimeric = i -> 
    new CellMetadata(i < 50 ? Algotype.BUBBLE : Algotype.INSERTION, ...);

engine.runUntilConvergence(10000);

// Result: Cells cluster by algotype WITHOUT explicit clustering code!
// Bubble cells migrate to one region, insertion cells to another.
```

**Real-world applications:**
- Agent-based modeling
- Swarm intelligence research
- Self-organizing systems

#### 3. Observable Delayed Gratification

Some problems require temporary setbacks for long-term progress. EDE makes this visible:

```java
// Track disorder over time
for (int step = 0; step < 100; step++) {
    engine.step();
    double disorder = monotonicity.compute(cells);
    System.out.println("Step " + step + ": " + disorder);
}

// Output shows disorder INCREASES before final convergence!
// Step 20: 45% disordered
// Step 40: 52% disordered (worse!)
// Step 80: 12% disordered (rapid improvement)
```

**Real-world applications:**
- Understanding biological development
- Multi-objective optimization
- Strategy evolution research

#### 4. Domain-Agnostic Framework

Implement `Comparable<T>` and EDE works for ANY problem:

```java
// Integer factorization (beyond sorting!)
public class FactorCell implements Cell<FactorCell> {
    @Override
    public int compareTo(FactorCell other) {
        return Integer.compare(this.remainder, other.remainder);
    }
}

// Same engine, different problem domain!
```

**Real-world applications:**
- Prototyping emergent algorithms for new domains
- Cross-domain research (biology ↔ computation)
- Educational tool for emergence concepts

### The Biological Inspiration

EDE models how biological systems achieve goals through **decentralized coordination**:

- Embryonic cells organize into organs without blueprints
- Ant colonies solve complex problems through simple local rules  
- Slime molds navigate mazes via chemical signaling

These systems are **robust, adaptive, and emergent**. EDE brings these properties to computational problems.

### When to Use EDE

✅ **Use EDE when you need:**
- Fault tolerance (unreliable substrates)
- Emergent pattern detection (clustering, segregation)  
- Observable dynamics (delayed gratification, trajectories)
- Cross-domain algorithm research
- Educational demonstrations of emergence

❌ **Don't use EDE when you need:**
- Maximum runtime performance (`Arrays.sort()` wins)
- Simple, one-off sorting tasks
- Guaranteed O(n log n) complexity
- Production-critical code without experimental tolerance

author: learnerlj
body:
## 概述

改进 CRS（Claude Relay Service）同步功能：
1. **增强错误信息**，便于诊断问题
2. **私有 IP 白名单支持**，适配内网 CRS 部署
3. **灵活配置方式**，支持 config.yaml 和环境变量

---

## 改动说明

### 1. API 错误处理增强

**接口**: `/api/v1/admin/accounts/sync/crs`  
**文件**: `backend/internal/handler/admin/account_handler.go:358`

**改进前**:
```json
{
  "code": 500,
  "message": "internal error"
}
```

**改进后**:
```json
{
  "code": 500,
  "message": "CRS sync failed: Post \"https://****/web/auth/login\": resolved ip 10.x.x.x is not allowed"
}
```

✅ 管理员现在可以看到具体的错误原因，而不是泛泛的"内部错误"

---

### 2. 安全配置

新增环境变量 `SECURITY_URL_ALLOWLIST_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS`：

**生产环境** (`docker-compose.yml`)：
- 默认值: `false`（默认安全）
- 阻止私有 IP（10.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x, 127.x.x.x）

**测试环境** (`docker-compose-test.yml`)：
- 默认值: `true`（方便内网测试）
- 允许私有 IP 访问

**使用方式**：
```bash
# 在 .env 文件中设置
SECURITY_URL_ALLOWLIST_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS=true
```

---

### 3. 灵活配置支持

在生产和测试环境都添加了 `config.yaml` 挂载支持：

```yaml
volumes:
  - ./config.yaml:/app/data/config.yaml:ro
```

**配置优先级**：
```
环境变量 > config.yaml > 默认值
```

**使用场景**：
- 📝 使用 `config.yaml` 进行详细/复杂配置
- ⚡ 使用环境变量快速覆盖
- 🎛️ 混合使用以获得最大灵活性

---

## 应用场景

适用于 CRS 服务器部署在**内网/私有网络**的情况，CRS 服务器域名解析到私有 IP 地址，同时在生产环境保持默认安全设置。

**示例**：
- CRS 服务器: `internal-crs.company.local`
- 解析到: `10.144.0.3`（私有 IP）
- 解决方案: 设置 `SECURITY_URL_ALLOWLIST_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS=true`

Snyk has created this PR to upgrade react from 19.1.0 to 19.2.3.

:information_source: Keep your dependencies up-to-date. This makes it easier to fix existing vulnerabilities and to more quickly identify and fix newly disclosed vulnerabilities when they affect your project.
- The recommended version is **147 versions** ahead of your current version. - The recommended version was released **24 days ago**.
Release notes
Package name: react
  • 19.2.3 - 2025-12-11

    React Server Components

    • Add extra loop protection to React Server Functions (@ sebmarkbage #35351)
  • 19.2.2 - 2025-12-11

    React Server Components

    • Move react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled to private react-server-dom-unbundled (@ eps1lon #35290)
    • Patch Promise cycles and toString on Server Functions (@ sebmarkbage, @ unstubbable #35289, #35345)
  • 19.2.1 - 2025-12-03

    React Server Components

    • Bring React Server Component fixes to Server Actions (@ sebmarkbage #35277)
  • 19.2.0 - 2025-10-01

    Below is a list of all new features, APIs, and bug fixes.

    Read the React 19.2 release post for more information.

    New React Features

    • <Activity>: A new API to hide and restore the UI and internal state of its children.
    • useEffectEvent is a React Hook that lets you extract non-reactive logic into an Effect Event.
    • cacheSignal (for RSCs) lets your know when the cache() lifetime is over.
    • React Performance tracks appear on the Performance panel’s timeline in your browser developer tools

    New React DOM Features

    • Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Web Streams:
      • resume: to resume a prerender to a stream.
      • resumeAndPrerender: to resume a prerender to HTML.
    • Added resume APIs for partial pre-rendering with Node Streams:
      • resumeToPipeableStream: to resume a prerender to a stream.
      • resumeAndPrerenderToNodeStream: to resume a prerender to HTML.
    • Updated prerender APIs to return a postponed state that can be passed to the resume APIs.

    Notable changes

    • React DOM now batches suspense boundary reveals, matching the behavior of client side rendering. This change is especially noticeable when animating the reveal of Suspense boundaries e.g. with the upcoming <ViewTransition> Component. React will batch as much reveals as possible before the first paint while trying to hit popular first-contentful paint metrics.
    • Add Node Web Streams (prerender, renderToReadableStream) to server-side-rendering APIs for Node.js
    • Use underscore instead of : IDs generated by useId

    All Changes

    React

    • <Activity /> was developed over many years, starting before ClassComponent.setState (@ acdlite @ sebmarkbage and many others)
    • Stringify context as "SomeContext" instead of "SomeContext.Provider" (@ kassens #33507)

author: duber000
body:
This commit modernizes the codebase to use Python 3.9-3.14 features for better
readability, maintainability, and performance.

## Changes Made:

### 1. Type Hints Modernization (Python 3.9+)
- Replaced `Optional[Type]` → `Type | None` (PEP 604)
- Replaced `Tuple[int, int]` → `tuple[int, int]` (PEP 585)
- Replaced `List[Type]` → `list[Type]` (PEP 585)
- Replaced `Dict[K, V]` → `dict[K, V]` (PEP 585)
- Removed unnecessary `from typing import` statements

### 2. Pattern Matching (Python 3.10+)
- Added `match-case` statements in `ai_actions.py` for action dispatching
- Replaced `if-elif isinstance()` chains with pattern matching
- Affects: `validate_action()` and `execute_action()` methods
- Benefits: More readable, better performance, type-checker friendly

### 3. TypeAlias Annotations (Python 3.10+)
- Added explicit `TypeAlias` annotations in `shared/types.py`
- Added new `Position` type alias for `tuple[int, int]`
- Better IDE support and type checking

## Files Modified:
- `game/ai_actions.py`: Type hints + pattern matching
- `game/game_state.py`: Type hints modernization
- `game/generator.py`: Type hints modernization
- `shared/types.py`: Added TypeAlias annotations

## Documentation:
- Added comprehensive review document: `PYTHON_FEATURES_REVIEW.md`
- Documents all opportunities for Python 3.6-3.14 features
- Includes recommendations and implementation plan

## Testing:
- All modified files compile successfully
- Pattern matching validated with runtime tests
- Import validation successful
- Syntax fully compatible with Python 3.10+

## Impact:
- ~50 type hint updates across 4 files
- 2 critical pattern matching improvements
- No breaking changes to public APIs
- Improved code readability and maintainability
